display.title: The Alter Rebbe and the Stolen Logs, Part 1 (Chai Elul)
display.summary_short: For Chai Elul, the light of Chassidus in every part of life, a riddle about filling a room, and the start of the story of an honest Chassid framed for stealing logs.
display.summary_long: In the week of Chai Elul, the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, the storyteller explains that Chai Elul brings life into the work of Elul, and that Chassidus brings light into everything we do, even how we play and what we wear. He recalls standing near the Rebbe in 770 when the Rebbe pointed out the picture on a boy's shirt. A riddle follows: three brothers try to fill a room to the brim, with paper, then water, and finally with light. Then the story begins. Reb Baruch, a Chassid of the Alter Rebbe known for his honesty, is hired to manage the government lumberyard that cuts logs for the new railroad, working only six days and leaving early on Friday for Shabbos. Alex, the angry former manager, hides twenty stolen logs in Reb Baruch's barn and reports him. Summoned to the minister's office, Reb Baruch asks the Alter Rebbe what to do, and the Rebbe only tells him to come back next Sunday. To be continued.
display.lesson: Chassidus fills every part of life with light, and a Chassid trusts a tzaddik's instructions even when he cannot see the way out.

date.note: 'A very special week that has Chai Elul'; year inferred from the next part (COVID, before Rosh Hashanah) and part 3 (Vov Tishrei 5781).

advisories.note: Reb Baruch fears the summons could mean prison, Siberia or death.

sources_cited.note: A letter of the Frierdiker Rebbe: children should play nicely and speak clean words at recess.

other_personal.text: Storyteller says the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to his grandfather, then living in Pittsburgh, to be home two hours before Shabbos.
